implementation_notes: EF Core calls this an owned entity type, and it is dependent mapping by construction: configure the child collection with OwnsMany (or mark the type [Owned]) and there is no DbSet for it, instances cannot be shared by two owners, and owned types are loaded with the owner by default and saved through it; their key is a shadow property composed of the owner key and a surrogate. Nothing else is required unless another consumer must query the child with its own SQL - then a hand-written repository (Dapper over a transaction) that replaces the child rows is the fallback, and the child must be treated as an independent entity.
pitfalls: Owned types cannot be shared between owners and cannot be queried through a DbSet - code that needs 'all lines across orders' must drop to SQL or the model is wrong.
Querying the owner always includes its owned types (no Include needed), so a large dependent collection is loaded even when only the parent is used - project explicitly to avoid the over-fetch.
Cascading deletes of owned rows are wholesale: an external foreign key to a line row makes the replacement semantics invalid, so check the schema before adopting owned types.
